verdict.summary: Round 2 remains sound. The MCP update tool constructs one server QueryBudget and passes it through both WAC/ACP authorization and application. PodStore preserves the unlimited public entry points, bounds variable-GRAPH write-set resolution and WHERE-bearing application with the supplied budget, fails closed before application when authorization resolution exhausts it, and keeps budget errors distinct from permission denial. The tests exercise real authorized update paths with expired-budget failures, unlimited/generous positive controls, mutation checks, authorization-stage and apply-stage coverage, WAC/ACP parity, and the documented WHERE-less boundary. Documentation matches the non-atomic-on-apply-error contract and public skills are updated. No correctness, soundness, security, injection, or vacuous-test issue is evident. With zero findings in both rounds, progress is stagnant under the required scale.
